question: How many covalent bonds are present between the constituent atoms in the molecules of Butane and Hexane, respectively?
solution:
The correct answer is __**13 and 19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Butane (C₄H₁₀)**:

 
 
• Butane is an alkane with **4 carbon atoms** and **10 hydrogen atoms**.
 
• The molecular structure consists of single covalent bonds between carbon atoms and between carbon and hydrogen atoms.
 
• It forms **13 covalent bonds**:
 
 
• **3 single bonds** between adjacent carbon atoms.
 
• **10 single bonds** between carbon and hydrogen atoms.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Hexane (C₆H₁₄)**:
 
 
• Hexane is an alkane with **6 carbon atoms** and **14 hydrogen atoms**.
 
• Its molecular structure comprises single covalent bonds between carbon atoms and carbon-hydrogen bonds.
